The regulations do not apply to operations and reclamation on Indian lands except as may now or in the future be provided in separate regulations to be issued by the Bureau of Indian Affairs (25 CFR Chapter I). The BIA is currently drafting new regulations covering mining operations and reclamation for Indian coal. It is anticipated that at a minimum these new regulations will be as stringent as those contained in 30 CFR 211. In the interim period the operating and reclamation standards in 30 CFR 211.40 could be made applicable.
As discussed in Chapter I the State of Montana is expected to demand compliance with State Laws and Regulations in that the State has jurisdiction over the majority of surface rights in the Ceded Area. Thus the Westmoreland Resources operation, being on State administered surface lands, must also conform with the Montana Environmental Policy Act and the Montana Strip Mining and Reclamation Act. A comparison of State and Federal standards reveals that the information to be submitted with the mining plan is substantially the same. Exceptions are that the federal regulations require one drill hole analysis for every 40 acres, while state guidelines require drill hole analysis every 2,000 feet; federal regulations also require potassium and phosphoreous analysis on overburden.
